names.note: In the Chaco it is simply "el árbol". Often confused with the algarrobo negro (Neltuma nigra), with which it hybridises.

range_note: Gran Chaco and central Argentina (Córdoba among the provinces), Bolivia, Paraguay, Peru, Chile and Uruguay; in low, salty sites and where groundwater is near.

summary.es: Árbol del Chaco de tronco corto y copa ancha, redonda y liviana, de hojas bipinnadas finas. En primavera se llena de espigas amarillentas y en verano cuelgan sus vainas amarillas, dulces, que comen la gente y el ganado. Aguanta sequía y sal; necesita sol pleno.
summary.en: A Chaco tree with a short trunk and a wide, round, airy crown of fine bipinnate leaves. In spring it fills with yellowish flower spikes and in summer its sweet straw-yellow pods hang down, eaten by people and livestock. It stands drought and salt and needs full sun.

adult_height_m.note: 5–15 m (ICRAF, Wikipedia); 9–12 m in Córdoba (cba); up to 18 m (INTA). Tall trees are rare today because of logging.

crown_width_m.note: Sources give only the maximum, a globose crown up to 10 m across; min and typical read from the reference photos, where the crown is about as wide as the tree is tall or wider.

trunk_dbh_m.note: Up to 1 m (ICRAF, Wikipedia), 1.5 m (INTA); min and typical from the reference photos.

trunks.note: Short bole with many branches (ICRAF); short trunk (cba); the photos show one trunk forking low into two to four limbs, sometimes two or three stems.

leaf_out.note: New bright green leaves come with the first flowers.

flowering.note: iNaturalist flowering annotations: 2 in September, 12 in October, 6 in November; cba says August to September.

fruiting.note: iNaturalist fruit annotations: December 6, January 10, February 6, March 7, April 4. Ripe pods fall over the summer; some dry pods stay into autumn.

leaf_fall.note: Late and partial: it loses leaves in winter but is never fully bare (cba); 'caedizo tardío' (avesarg).

rainfall_mm_year.note: ICRAF's biophysical limits. In Argentina it also grows where rain is higher but the soil is salty or the groundwater near (INTA, ICRAF).

drought_tolerance.note: Very efficient with water; bears most fruit in drought years.

shade_tolerance_seedling.note: Heliophilous: needs direct sun to grow and develop.

frost_kill_c_adult.note: Stands several −5 °C freezes but not a 12-hour freeze below 0 °C (Felker); short dawn freezes near −11 °C do little harm. Wikipedia and cba say it does not tolerate frost well. How long the cold lasts matters more than how low it goes.

uses: Pods eaten fresh, as flour and as drinks (añapa, and aloja when fermented)
Pods stored as fodder for droughts
Timber for furniture, flooring, carpentry and casks
Bark and resin dye fibres; folk medicine
Shade in silvopastoral systems; windbreaks and street trees
